title: Factorization of the specified compact-support coefficient realization over an arbitrary field
statement:
Let $k$ be a field of positive characteristic $p$, let $\ell\ne p$ be prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite with valuation ring $R$, uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes and fix a compactification $c=(X\xrightarrow{j}Z\xrightarrow{g}Y)$, with $j$ open and $g$ proper [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. On their small pro-etale sites put $\widehat R_T=\lim_n(A_n)_T$ and use the completed integral constructible categories $\mathcal I_T(R)$, strict reduction $\mathcal R_T$, total limit $\mathcal L_T$ and actual unit $u$ of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete, lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Write $P_R$ and $\alpha_K:\mathcal R_YP_RK\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal F\mathcal R_XK$ for the specified compact-support reconstruction and system comparison of [lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization], with $\mathcal F=S_g\mathcal E_j$ the simultaneous proper/open system composite [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Put $P_R^0=Rg_{*,R}j_{!,R}$; it preserves these integral categories [lem-cbc-integral-compact-support-uniform-restriction].

Let $\rho_K:\mathcal R_YP_R^0K\to\mathcal F\mathcal R_XK$ be the actual system proper coefficient projection followed by the open scalar comparison, with the proper comparison the transpose of pullback/scalar balancing followed by the proper counit, and the open comparison the inverse open-unit adjunct of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. These are simultaneous derived system maps [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Identify $\mathcal L_Y\mathcal F\mathcal R_XK=P_RK$ through the defining strict tower. Then
$$q_K=\mathcal L_Y(\rho_K)u_{P_R^0K}:P_R^0K\xrightarrow{\sim}P_RK,\qquad \alpha_K\mathcal R_Y(q_K)=\rho_K.$$
When $g=\mathrm{id}_Y$, $P_R^0=j_{!,R}$ and $\rho_K=r_j(K)$ is precisely the comparison of [lem-sf-integral-open-reduction-comparison], after the identity direct-image factors are removed.

Use the derived scalar realization $J_T:\mathcal I_T(R)[1/t]\simeq\mathcal C_E^c(T)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization], and put $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ with its finite-extension-valued condensed ring [prop-weil-pbc-qbar-condensed-two-colimit]. For $F/E$ finite inside $\Omega$, or $F=\Omega$, let $T_T=F_T^c\otimes^L_{E_T^c}-$ and $P_D^c=Rg_{*,D}j_{!,D}$ for $D=E,F$. Write $\delta^J_j:J_Zj_{!,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{!,E}J_X$ and $\delta^{E,F}_j:T_Zj_{!,E}\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{!,F}T_X$ for the open scalar comparisons whose inverses are the specified open-unit adjuncts [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. Rationalization is understood in $\delta^J_j$. Let $\chi^J_g$ be the specified direct-image comparison of $J$ and $\pi_g:T_YRg_{*,E}\to Rg_{*,F}T_Z$ the proper coefficient counit mate [def-pur-condensed-compact-support-projection]. For every $K\in\mathcal I_X(R)$ the specified comparisons $a$ and $\xi$ of [lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization] satisfy
$$a_{f,E,K}=Rg_{*,E}(\delta^J_{j,K})\circ\chi^J_{g,j_{!,R}K}\circ J_Y(q_K^{-1}[1/t]),$$
$$\xi_{f,E,F,J_X(K[1/t])}=Rg_{*,F}(\delta^{E,F}_{j,J_X(K[1/t])})\circ\pi_{g,j_{!,E}J_X(K[1/t])}.$$
For $g=\mathrm{id}$, both proper factors $\chi^J_g$ and $\pi_g$ are the identity under the canonical direct-image unitors. All displayed equalities are natural in $K$ and hold in the indicated coefficient derived categories, including $F=\Omega$.

source.place: Definition 6.7.6, Lemma 6.7.7, Proposition 6.8.14(2), Remark 6.8.15 provide context only. Agent-formulated normalization of the comparison constructed in lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization, proof Steps 2–5, 6 and 13; not a literal assertion of Bhatt–Scholze.

proof.text: Check the integral inputs. The schemes $X,Y,Z$ are finite type over $k$ (for $Z$, use that $g$ is proper). They are noetherian and have finite dimension by the two cited finiteness results. Every open subscheme of $Z$ is quasi-compact by the cited open-subscheme result; applying this to opens inside affine opens of $Z$ makes $j$ quasi-compact. The characteristic condition makes $\ell$ invertible. Apply the integral compact-support restriction to $c$ and also to $(j,\mathrm{id}_Z)$. With $H=j_{!,R}K$ and $B=P_R^0K=Rg_{*,R}H$, it gives $H\in\mathcal I_Z(R)$ and $B\in\mathcal I_Y(R)$, hence both are derived complete. The completion-unit clause of the constant/completed equivalence identifies the actual quotient-tower unit $u_B:B\to\mathcal L_Y\mathcal R_YB$ with the completion unit, so $u_B$ is invertible.

source.place: Steps 2–3: integral comparison; integral input check corresponding to lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization, proof Step 1.

proof.text:
Put $N=\mathcal F\mathcal R_XK$. Construct $\rho_K$ on the ordinary derived ringed diagram topoi, as allowed by the simultaneous-system calculus. Its proper factor is the transpose of scalar balancing followed by the proper counit; its open factor is the inverse of the open-unit adjunct. Thus its evaluation is
$$(Rg_{*,R}H)\otimes^L_{\widehat R_Y}A_{n,Y}\longrightarrow Rg_{*,n}(H\otimes^L_{\widehat R_Z}A_{n,Z})\longrightarrow Rg_{*,n}j_{!,n}K_n.$$
The first arrow is precisely the projection-formula mate in the direct-image/limit theorem, with coefficient restriction identified by the ring-sheaf-change adjunction. Its hypotheses hold: $H$ is complete by Step 1, $R$ is a noetherian DVR, $R/t$ is additive torsion, and every $R/t^n$ is finite and perfect by the standard-quotients theorem. The coefficient inverse-image identifications are the specified projection-compatible ones. The second arrow is the open tensor normalization for $\widehat R\to A_n$, whose statement also applies to the entire coefficient diagram. Both evaluations are isomorphisms. Joint conservativity of system evaluation therefore makes $\rho_K$ an isomorphism of whole derived systems. No equality of arbitrary system arrows is inferred from evaluations.

source.place: Steps 2–3: actual compact-support map on reduction systems; explicit mate computation corresponding to lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization, proof Step 2.

proof.text: Identify $\mathcal L_YN=P_RK$ using the defining strict tower, as in the statement. This is an identification of the simultaneous construction: reduction on one flat-term K-flat complex, exact system open extension, separately derived system proper image, and coefficient restriction. The strict-tower functor and the completed pushforward comparison identify these composites including transitions and maps. Write $e$ for the counit of $\mathcal R_Y\dashv\mathcal L_Y$. The specified $\alpha_K$ is $e_N$: both are constructed by taking the actual total-limit projection of this strict diagram and its scalar-extension adjunct on the simultaneous system resolutions. This identifies their defining derived-system transformation, rather than appealing to faithfulness of evaluations. The evaluation-calculus theorem gives exactly this normalization of $e_N$. Define $q_K=\mathcal L_Y(\rho_K)u_B$. Both factors are isomorphisms, by Steps 1–2 and functoriality of $\mathcal L_Y$.

source.place: Steps 2–3: unfolding the specified strict-tower realization and projection normalization; lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization, proof Step 3, with the actual counit identified explicitly.

proof.text:
For completeness, compute the requested system equation before taking any evaluation. Counit naturality at $\rho_K:\mathcal R_YB\to N$ gives
$$e_N\mathcal R_Y\mathcal L_Y(\rho_K)=\rho_K e_{\mathcal R_YB}.$$
Functoriality and the left triangle identity now give
$$\alpha_K\mathcal R_Y(q_K)=e_N\mathcal R_Y\mathcal L_Y(\rho_K)\mathcal R_Y(u_B)=\rho_K e_{\mathcal R_YB}\mathcal R_Y(u_B)=\rho_K.$$
These are the unit/counit identities in the derived system category supplied by the evaluation-calculus statement.

source.place: Step 2: triangle-identity calculation for the specified reconstruction unit.

proof.text: When $g=\mathrm{id}_Y$, remove the canonical direct-image unitors. The proper coefficient transpose is then scalar balancing followed by the identity counit, hence the identity. The remaining $\rho_K$ is the simultaneous open tensor comparison. The open-reduction theorem constructs $r_j(K)$ by this same extension by zero of a flat-term K-flat reduction representative with its strict quotient maps. Its final sentence fixes the same simultaneous section construction; the open tensor theorem fixes its inverse as the open-unit adjunct. Thus $\rho_K=r_j(K)$ as derived-system maps, not merely after evaluation. In particular $P_R^0=j_{!,R}$ and $q_K^{-1}=u_{j_{!,R}K}^{-1}\mathcal L_Y(r_j(K))^{-1}=d_j(K)$, with precisely the normalization of that theorem.

source.place: Steps 2–3: identity proper factor and open normalization.

proof.text:
Unpack the specified realization comparison $a$, retaining its map and not just its endpoints. On the integral model the specified passage from the reconstructed compact-support object to the ordinary compactification composite is $q_K^{-1}$ of Step 3. Applying rationalization and $J_Y$ gives $J_Y(q_K^{-1}[1/t])$. The next arrow is $\chi^J_{g,H}$: the direct-image comparison of the scalar realization, whose statement fixes compatibility with the pullback/direct-image counits. The remaining arrow is $Rg_{*,E}(\delta^J_{j,K})$. Indeed $J$ is derived extension from $\widehat R$ to $E^c$, and the open tensor theorem identifies its open comparison by the inverse open-unit adjunct. These are, in this order, the three arrows used to construct the specified $a$ in the source construction (proof Steps 4–5 of lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization). Substitution therefore gives
$$a_{f,E,K}=Rg_{*,E}(\delta^J_{j,K})\circ\chi^J_{g,H}\circ J_Y(q_K^{-1}[1/t]).$$
This is an unfolding of the specified construction plus Step 3's identification of its reconstruction arrow; it is not an inference that arbitrary isomorphisms with these endpoints agree.

source.place: Steps 2–3: expansion of the specified rational realization; source construction lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization, proof Steps 4–5.

proof.text:
For $L=J_X(K[1/t])$, the specified $\xi_{f,E,F,L}$ is the canonical coefficient projection comparison for the chosen compactification. By the definition of this projection, paste its proper counit mate at $j_{!,E}L$ with proper image of its open scalar comparison. The open tensor theorem identifies the latter comparison with $\delta^{E,F}_{j,L}$, because their inverses are the same open-unit adjunct. Thus, in the $F$-coefficient derived category,
$$\xi_{f,E,F,L}=Rg_{*,F}(\delta^{E,F}_{j,L})\circ\pi_{g,j_{!,E}L}.$$
This calculation also applies directly to $F=\Omega$: the projection definition expressly includes the finite-extension-valued algebraic-closure coefficient ring. Its ring and scalar extension are those in the two-colimit theorem, and the compact-support realization theorem identifies its canonical coefficient projection as an isomorphism as well. No interchange of unbounded direct image and filtered colimit is needed to prove this factorization.

source.place: Steps 2–3: specified coefficient comparison; source construction lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization, proof Steps 6 and 13.

proof.text: For $g=\mathrm{id}$, the direct-image adjunction is the identity adjunction under its canonical unitors. Consequently the counit-preserving direct-image comparison $\chi^J_g$ becomes the identity: its transpose is the scalar pullback identification followed by the identity counit. The same transpose calculation makes $\pi_g$ the identity for either finite $F$ or $F=\Omega$. Every arrow used above is a specified natural transformation (reduction unit/counit, system coefficient mate, open scalar comparison, or realization comparison). Functors preserve their compositions and inverses of their isomorphism components. Hence the displayed equations are natural in $K$ and lie in the stated coefficient derived categories. The argument did not require $k$ to be algebraically closed or finite. For the Lean declaration q_naturality, use the proved fixedOpenReduction_isIso helper of OpenReconstructionEffectivity on every integral object. Thus inverseOrZero of openReduction is the component of its inverse natural transformation. Form the proper reduction transformation from the reduction unit, the inverse proper-limit presentation and the reduction counit; paste its open inverse and canonical system presentation to obtain rhoTransformation. Whisker this with total limit, precede it by the actual reduction unit and follow it by limitPresentation.inv to obtain qTransformation. Its component equation is the specified q, so its naturality square is exactly q_naturality, without any quasi-compactness, finite-Tor-window or invertibility assumptions added to the statement. The three identity-normalization declarations and the main existence declaration retain their original proof obligations.
